notes.decision: Parsed as 'they themselves / they also' (intensive pronoun ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲩ + emphatic ⲟⲛ 'also'). Closes the previous clause identifying Saklas and his companion as the very molders of Adam and Eve, before the new sentence opens with 'The icon...' Alternative parsing 'they brought' (ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲩ-ⲉⲓⲛⲉ → ⲟⲛ) is grammatically possible.
Greek κατὰ ταῦτα 'according to these things, in like manner'. Rendered 'According to these things' to preserve the Greek discourse-marker function.

Translated 'they applied (it)'. The verb appears to combine the giving-sense of ϯ with possible -ⲍ suffix (3sg.f) — but here applied to a seal-imprint, the contextually appropriate sense is 'applied/stamped/impressed'. The icon's imprint is applied to the molding of Adam and Eve. Alternative 'they joined' (ⲧⲱϩ̄/ⲧⲱⲍ).

Translated 'has gushed forth'. Lyc. verb of unclear root governing 'from the archons' as source. Best fit is a verb of cosmic emanation/gushing, paralleling ⲃⲉⲃⲉ 'gush' in Manichaean cosmogony of the abortions/Hyle bursting from the archons. Confidence moderate.

The bare ⲛⲥ̄ on lines 12 and bracketing line 13 represents the kephalaion number in Greek numerals — ν (50) + ϛ/stigma (6) = 56 — functioning both as chapter-number and as decorative ornament around the chapter title. Standard Manichaean Kephalaia formatting convention.

Translated 'she spoke through the chief archon, their Principality' — taking ϩⲙ̄ as instrumental ('through, by means of'). Hyle/Concupiscence (the implicit feminine subject) speaks through the archonic voice; the apposition 'their Principality' identifies which archon (the chief / leader of the principalities). ⲁⲛⲝⲱⲝ confirmed in accumulated vocabulary as 'principalities/leading-powers.'

ⲁⲩⲉⲓⲥ rendered as plural imperative 'Come you!' (= Sah. ⲁⲙⲏⲉⲓⲧⲛ̄). The intervening ⲙⲁ⸓ contains the editor's symbol ⸓ which I have left as-is — possibly an abbreviation marker or scribal symbol. ⲛϩⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲡⲉ taken as 'unto heaven' (ⲛ̄- directional + ⲍⲏⲓ 'into' + ⲛ̄ⲧⲡⲉ 'of heaven'); cf. parallel cosmogonic narratives where archons resolve to ascend.

ⲧⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ taken as exclamation/vocative 'Our light!' (1pl possessive). ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ as 1pl conjunctive 'let us fashion.' ⲛⲏⲧⲛⲉ is dative 2pl 'for yourselves' — the chief archon addresses fellow archons inclusively. The construction is unusual (1pl verb + 2pl beneficiary) and may reflect group-internal address.

Parsed as ⲛⲁϥ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟϥ ⲇⲉ ϩⲱⲱϥ — 'for him; but he himself.' The contrast is between collective archonic action and individual creator-act. ⲁⲉ = ⲇⲉ adversative; ⲛⲉϩ/ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ/ϩⲱⲱϩ form the standard Lyc. 'for him / he / himself' triplet.

Capitalized 'Sin' as cosmic principle per terminology guide. ⲃⲁⲃϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ rendered 'poured forth' — the verb (Lyc. reflex of ⲃⲱϩ/ⲃⲱⲱⲃ) suggests gushing/outpouring. The image is of Sin emanating outward, anticipating the identification with Hyle in the following clause.

Antithetical parallelism 'some in likeness, some not in likeness' — referring to the offspring begotten by the archons: some bear the likeness (of the Exalted One captured through the fruits), others do not. ⲉϩⲉⲓⲛⲉ = ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'in the likeness'; the negation ⲉⲛ closes the second clause. Translation preserves the parallel structure.

Translated 'a sense-faculty and an operation' — keeping the Greek loanwords αἴσθησις and ἐνέργεια in their technical sense. The molder has placed members on the outside and inside, AND a perception-faculty AND an operative-power — the dual interior endowment that allows the body's storehouses to function.

Future relative with 3pl object suffix. Tentatively rendered 'they shall match them' from a verb of comparison/equation (cf. ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲧ 'compare'). The correspondential register of this passage (sense-organs draw external objects in, store them, produce them on demand to match interior storehouse contents) supports a verb of correspondence-establishment. Confidence moderate — could alternatively be a verb of transferring/joining.

ⲡⲁⲓⲧⲏⲧⲏⲥ = Greek αἰτητής 'one who demands/asks' — the body's recurrent appetitive demand. ⲉⲧⲱⲓⲧⲉ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ 'who claims/demands them.' ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ tentatively 'continually' (Lyc. adverb), though could be a separate clause-tag. Renders the body's senses as servants delivering up stored material to a perpetual demander.

Translated 'nature' (Greek φύσις). The chapter is structured around the φύσις of each sense-faculty (eyes, ears, smell) as a personified feminine entity with houses, treasuries, and chambers. The 'nature' is the inner-cosmic structure of the sensory-storage apparatus.

Translated 'shafts' for ϣⲁϩ — the third architectural element after houses (ⲏⲓ̈) and treasuries (ⲁⲡⲟⲫⲏⲕⲏ). Coptic ϣⲁϩ can mean 'pit, shaft, hollow.' Functions as the deepest layer of internal storage.
Translated 'Again the time when' — circumstantial relative construction introducing a temporal clause about the φύσις acting upon stored impressions.

Translated 'is drawn in heart.' ⲏⲕ qualitative likely from a verb of approach/inclination (cf. ⲱⲕⲙ̄/ⲱⲕⲉ family). Combined with ⲁ̄ⲧⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'to look out at' = the eye-faculty inclines/yearns inwardly toward the stored likeness.
ⲁⲥ-ⲝⲓ-ⲧϩ 'she-take/carry-it' (Lyc. ϫⲓ + 3sg.m suffix). Recurring verb of the page (segments 4, 7, 16, 20, 26) — the technical verb for the faculty's act of conveying impressions inward to storage.

Conjunctive ⲛ̄ⲥ- + ⲛ̄ⲧ + 3pl/3sg suffix + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' = 'and she brings them/it forth.' The retrieval-verb complementing ⲁⲥⲝⲓⲧϩ (storage). The pair establishes a complete carrying-in/bringing-out cycle.
ⲉⲓⲧⲉ Greek 'whether'; ⲃⲉ uncertain — possibly emphatic particle or scribal element. Translated minimally as 'whether either' to preserve the disjunctive force without speculative addition.
ϯ 'gives' + ⲛ̄ⲥ- conjunctive + ⲣⲧⲍⲉ 'do likewise' = 'gives, doing in like manner.' Iterative formula introducing the type-mapping: each sense-faculty operates on the same pattern.
Greek τύπος 'type, figure' — translated 'this type' (per glossary). The technical exegetical term for the typological correspondence between the three sense-faculties' processes.
'Ten of hundred(s) of days' = 1000 days. The temporal extent of the ear-faculty's storage period before retrieval. Numeric construction ⲙⲏⲧ (10) + ϣⲉ (hundred) + ⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ (days).
Temporal clause 'when one comes to seek' — ⲛⲧⲉ-ⲟⲩⲉ 'when one' + ⲉⲛⲩ̄ (ⲉ-ⲛⲏⲩ 'coming') + ϣⲛ̄ (ϣⲓⲛⲉ 'seek'); verb split across line break 19/20.

ⲡⲓⲧⲱϣ 'this boundary/portion' repeated as a structural marker — first closing the previous section (ear-faculty), then opening the new one (smell-faculty). Standard chapter-internal sectioning device.

ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ϣⲱⲗⲙ ('smell') = 'the place of smelling' — the olfactory faculty named in the same compound pattern as ⲙⲁⲛⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'place of hearing' in line 26. Direct correspondence with bodily organ as cosmic locus.
Compound ⲣⲉϥ- + ϣⲓⲛⲉ = 'the inquirer/asker.' Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' The figure who petitions the storage-faculty for retrieval of an impression.

ⲡ- + ⲣ̄- + ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ ('thought/memory') = 'the remembrance' or 'the act of remembering.' The retrieved impression as memory delivered to the petitioner. Built on ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ (per glossary, second of the five faculties = ennoia).

Translated 'Such also is this' — the discourse marker Ⲧ̄ϩⲉ (= Lyc. variant of ⲧϩⲉ 'manner') opens a typological-correspondence statement applying the foregoing schema to the body's enthumesis. Pattern recurs in lines 5, 10, 17.

Translated 'enthumesis of the body,' retaining the Greek loanword (ἐνθύμησις) untranslated to preserve its technical Manichaean register as the body's discriminating-storing faculty (counterpart to the cosmic ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ 'counsel' in the five-faculty mapping per Polotsky/Böhlig). Here it operates as the inner organizing faculty receiving sense-impressions.

Rendered ⲡⲓⲱⲣϩ as 'the sight' (the seeing-faculty / what is looked at), with ⲛⲁⲓ̈ⲁⲣϩϥ̄ as Lyc. future of ⲱⲣϩ̄ 'look at, watch.' Same root as accumulated ⲡⲓ̈ⲱⲣϩ 'the watcher' (agent-noun) but here in passive-object register: the sight is what the eyes look at and convey inward to the enthumesis.

Lyc. ⲛ̄-ⲥⲉ-ϫⲓ-ⲧ-ϥ 'and they take it' — ϫⲓ 'take, receive' with 3sg.m. object. Recurs throughout this passage as the verb of the senses' transfer-action (eyes/ears take the impression and hand it over to the enthumesis).

Tentatively rendered 'the grasping of the hands' for the touch/feel sense, completing the five-sense enumeration (sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch). ⲡⲟⲁⲙⲟⲙ̄ is unattested in our corpus; possibly a Lyc. reduplicated form related to ⲱⲙ 'seize, swallow' or ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'grasp.' ⲛⲟⲓⲝ = Lyc. plural of ϭⲓϫ 'hand.' Confidence low on the verbal noun's etymology, but contextually certain that this is the touch-faculty.

Translated 'some watchmen' tentatively. ⲁⲛ-ⲟⲩ-ⲣⲙϣⲉ analyzed as Lyc. indefinite plural ⲁⲛ- (= ϩⲛ̄-) + ⲟⲩ- + ⲣⲙϣⲉ. The element ⲣⲙϣⲉ is unclear — possibly a Lyc. compound 'watchman / man of the post' (cf. ⲣⲙ-, 'person of' + ϣⲉ 'wood, stake'?), or a corruption of ⲟⲩⲣⲏⲏϣⲉ. Context (men set upon gates, with nets and guards) confirms a watching/gate-keeping function.

Translated 'nets set' for ϣⲁϣⲧ 'nets, snares' (Crum 605b ϣⲁϣⲧ̄ 'a snare') with ⲁⲧⲃ̄ tentatively as qualitative of ⲱⲧⲡ̄/ⲱⲡⲧ̄ 'shut, joined, set.' The image of nets-at-the-gate fits the parable of selective admission (citizens through, strangers blocked). Cf. line 19-20 'with the nets at the mouths of the gates.'
Mid-line break starts a new structural unit (the parable proper, after the break_after on segment 18). 'Just as some watchmen who keep watch over encampments...' opens the comparative parable.

Translated 'according to their purpose of heart' per accumulated glossary entry ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'purpose/intention.' The watchmen admit fellow-citizens according to their (the city's/their own) deliberative will — fits the cognitive-allegorical reading where the gates are the body's senses regulated by the heart's purpose.

Greek loanword συγχωρέω 'concede, permit' negated with Lyc. habitual ⲙⲁⲩ-. 'They do not permit him to enter' — strangers are kept at the door of the body (= the gates of the senses), an allegorical reading consistent with Manichaean ascetic teaching about regulated sense-input.

Tentatively translated 'the assemblage(?)' — ⲧⲏⲡⲧⲥ̄ from ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' qualitative-feminine = 'that which is reckoned/numbered.' In context with 'nets of the gates' may denote the assembled/counted set of gate-nets. Reading uncertain due to surrounding lacunae.

Rendered 'him who abides' from a tentative qualitative of ⲗⲟ 'stop, remain, abide.' The text is physically present (with diacritic) but the lexeme is uncertain. In context, 'him who abides within him' fits as a designation of the resident soul/Mind in whose body the gates exist.
Rendered 'the Illuminator says' — speech-introducing formula. The unusual ⲧ̄- onset may be scribal for ⲡ̄ⲧⲁⲭⲉ/ⲡⲉϫⲉ.

Rendered 'places of seeing.' ⲙⲁⲛ- 'place of' + ⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ 'see/watch' — parallel formation to ⲙⲁⲛⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ ('places of hearing') and ⲙⲁⲛϣⲱⲗⲙⲉ ('places of smelling'). The body's sense-faculties as topological gates.

Rendered 'those that look out' as the fourth sense-organ in the list. Possibly the eyes as 'sending-forth-of-sight,' though could also be 'those that send forth' (organs of breath/utterance). Uncertainty noted.
Rendered 'helpers' from probable analysis ⲣⲉϥⲣ̄-ⲡⲱϣⲉ 'one who shares/helps.' Parallel to phylakes in the list of beings stationed at the body's gates. Tentative.

Rendered 'to help them' — same root as line 8 'helpers' (ⲣ̄-ⲡⲱϣ 'help'). Could alternatively be parsed differently, but the contextual fit (continuing the action of the watching guards) supports this reading.

notes.coptic_form: ⲧⲉⲛⲑⲩⲙⲏⲥⲓⲥ ... ⲉⲧⲉ ⲛⲧⲁⲥ ⲡⲉ ⲧⲥⲃⲱ ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ
notes.decision: Rendered 'the enthumesis ... which is the teaching of the body.' Per the terminology guide, ⲧⲥⲃⲱ MUST be 'teaching' (not 'insight'/'prudence'). The passage is a correspondential identification: the cosmic/inner enthumesis functions as the body's instructional principle, the queen of its encampment.
Rendered 'they take charge of the encircling.' ⲁⲣⲭⲟⲩ from Greek ἄρχω 'rule, take charge.' The archons claim governance over the body's circuit and exclude the Mind as a stranger.
Rendered 'keys.' Best contextual fit: the Mind takes the means of opening/closing from the gate-guards, completing the metaphor. Crum attests ϣⲁϣⲧ as a noun in this semantic field.
Rendered 'to scoop inward.' ⲡⲱⲛⲕ̄ 'scoop, draw out' (cf. accumulated vocabulary entry ⲡⲁⲛⲕ). Preserves the inward-directional semantics characteristic of Manichaean cosmological prepositions.
Rendered 'that-which-begins to take.' ⲟⲩⲱ here as 'begin/proceed' (with infinitive complement ⲉϩϫⲓ 'to take'). Could alternatively read 'that-which-adds' (ⲟⲩⲱϩ).
Rendered 'the hands.' Likely ⲛ̄-ϭⲓϫ 'the hands' with intrusive ⲟ̄. The keys of the gates are 'under the hands' of the Mind = under his control.
Rendered 'his eyes.' Lyc. ⲛⲉϩ- 'his' + ⲃⲉⲗ (= ⲃⲁⲗ 'eye') in plural. Cf. accumulated ⲛⲓⲁⲧⲉ 'the eyes.'
Rendered 'luxury' (Greek τρυφή). Best contextual fit: the gate's 'lookouts of luxury/delight' opposed to righteousness. The Mind shuts the body off from such inputs.

Translated as 'taming.' Recurs at lines 5 and 13 as the structurally pivotal phrase ⲧⲇⲁⲙ ⲙ̄ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the taming of the Mind of Light' marking the turn from BEFORE to NOW. Likely from Greek δάμασις/δαμάζω 'tame, subdue,' fitting the Manichaean doctrine of the Light-Mind subduing the body's passions. Alternative: Coptic ⲧⲱⲙ 'shut, bind' (cf. line 26 'bound them in a bond of peace'). 'Taming' preserves the active subjugation semantics.

Parsed as ⲡⲉⲧⲁϩ- (perfect relative 'who has') + reduplicated verb (ϩ)ⲗⲱⲗⲙ̄ⲗⲱⲙ̄/ⲗⲱⲗⲙ̄ⲥ 'trample, defile' (in glossary as ⲗⲱⲗⲙ̄ⲥ/ϩⲟⲗⲙⲗⲱⲙⲥ̄) + 3pl object suffix -ⲩ. Translation 'who has trampled them down' fits the soteriological subjugation of the body's desires.

Translated 'the tyrant of the body.' Likely Lyc. nativized form of Greek τύραννος, with vowel-shift τυραν > ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲣⲉ. Apposition with ⲧⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ 'desire' identifies desire as the tyrant whom the Mind of Light has now humbled.

Translated 'have fled.' Recurs at line 15 (ⲁⲩⲣⲃⲁⲧⲉ 'they fled'). Likely Lyc. reflex of ⲣ̄-ⲡⲱⲧ 'do running, flee' or related to ⲡⲱⲱⲧⲉ 'leap.' Soteriological-cosmological motif: phantasies of desire and evil mysteries flee at the coming of the Mind of Light.

Translated 'persuasions.' Etymology uncertain — possibly Greek πειθώ 'persuasion' or πάθος 'passion' with Lyc. orthographic adaptation. Parallel with preceding ⲟⲩⲭⲗⲉ (= ὄχλος 'noise/crowd') of desire suggests an auditory-affective register. 'Persuasions' captures the seductive-rhetorical force fitting the ear-faculty context.

Translated 'it pleases (him) not at all ... it pleases (him).' The form ⲉⲍⲛⲉϩ likely from ϩⲛⲁ⸗ 'be pleased, wish' as impersonal predicate with ⲉⲛ negation. Antithetical pair structuring the contrast: hearings of desire are no longer welcome, voices of psalms are now welcome at every hour.

Translated 'songs.' Position between ⲡⲥⲁⲗⲙⲟⲥ 'psalms' and ⲍⲩⲙⲛⲟⲥ 'hymns' parallels the canonical NT triad ψαλμοί / ὕμνοι / ᾠδαί (Eph 5:19, Col 3:16). Possible Greek source: ᾠδαί 'songs/odes,' though phonological mapping is irregular. Could alternatively be a Coptic-specific liturgical term for antiphons/responses.

Translated 'one set above it.' Probable parsing ⲡⲉⲧ-ϩⲓ-ϫⲱ-ϥ̄ 'the one upon him,' i.e. 'overseer, restrainer.' The Manichaean theme: under the body's pre-conversion regime, Sin reigned with no one to restrain it; now the Living Spirit has become its lord (line 25).

Translated 'the first and the last.' Refers to Sin's former dominion as totality 'from beginning to end,' setting up the antithesis with the Holy Spirit's purpose-of-heart in line 32. Could alternatively be construed as a temporal partition: 'Sin's purpose was the first (former state); and (now) the purpose of the Holy Spirit (is) the last (final state) joined to the gnōmē of the Mind of Light.'

Retained as 'gnōmē' (Greek γνώμη 'judgment, mind, will'). Manichaean technical sense: the rational-judging will of the Mind of Light, which now governs in place of Sin's purpose-of-heart. Distinct from ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ (purpose) and ⲙⲉⲩⲉ (thought).

Translated as imperative 'take charge over yourselves' — Greek ἄρχω ('rule, take charge') with 2pl reflexive ⲧⲏⲛⲉ. The construction with ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲱⲧⲉ as adverbial complement gives 'exercise rule in/over the encompassing of the bodily men' — the apostolic-pastoral charge over the bodily community of disciples.

ⲛⲉ taken as negative future-prohibitive: 'so that Sin shall not become strong.' The whole Sin-clause governs five consecutive ⲛϥ̄- conjunctives describing what Sin would do if it prevailed: take light, scatter forth, spread forth.
Rendered 'from the All to the All' — the doubled ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ functions as merism for total/complete preparation, paralleling Manichaean cosmic-totality vocabulary already in glossary.
